{{Recipe summary
| Category = Bean recipes
| Servings = 10
| Difficulty = 2
}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Texas cuisine|Texas Cuisine]]

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] (450 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) dry [[Cookbook:Pinto Bean|pinto beans]]
*8 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] ground black [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*1 ham bone or a rough equivalent of salt bacon
*1–2 [[Cookbook:Bay leaf|bay leaves]]
*5 cups [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
*A very small amount (3 oz / ~90 g) of that day's brewed [[Cookbook:Coffee|coffee]] (optional)

==Procedure==
#Wash beans carefully and [[Cookbook:Soaking Beans|soak]] overnight in 8 cups of water.  
#Drain and refill with 5 cups of water.  
#Add all the other ingredients. 
#Bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] at least 1 hour, or until tender.  
#Remove bay leaves.  
#Do not drain prior to serving, the liquid is an important aspect of the dish.
#Can be served using slotted spoon, to allow draining, or with a ladle into small side-dish bowls   

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* The beans and the liquid can be ladled on to dry, stored cornbread (which, otherwise, can be exceptionally dry for eating purposes). The combination is very traditional.
